answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The canyon multiplier is published, charged in ledge, and meadow lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 3320 identities would post 788 proofs and burn roughly 2 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
